gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states Mobile Pixels' own cable order for its DS slide-out screens: USB-C to C alone first, then USB-C plus HDMI, then USB-C through the USB-A adapter plus HDMI, so a laptop whose USB-C port carries no video runs the screen on two cables, not one.
standout_why: Compared against shop.pcworld.com (cited, Duex Lite) and thedadsneeze.com (result 12, not cited). PCWorld Shop already gives the USB-A adapter plus HDMI path and 'Note: Driver required' for the Duex Lite. thedadsneeze already tells readers to check for DisplayPort Alt Mode, that the lid and hinge carry the extender, that the metal plates stay stuck to the lid, and the one-display limit on base M1/M2/M3 MacBooks. Neither gives the maker's three-step cable order for the DS models. The most-cited page, mobilepixels.us/products/duex-ds-series, returned HTTP 429 on six attempts today, so I could not check whether it already states this; Dealectric's own record for the Duex Max DS already carries 'USB-C plus HDMI for laptops without it'. thexebec.com/products/snap also returned 429.
decides: It does not change the pick; it qualifies it. The 1.3 lb Duex Plus DS and 1.8 lb Duex Max DS (weights as quoted on thedadsneeze, not re-read on the maker's page today) are one-cable screens only on a laptop whose USB-C port outputs video. On any other laptop the maker's Max DS guide adds an HDMI cable, so the travel kit grows by a second cable. The DS line also separates from the older Duex Lite that ChatGPT showed at the same 1.3 lb: PCWorld Shop's Lite listing says 'Driver required' and Mobile Pixels' Duex FAQ walks through reinstalling a DisplayLink driver, which matters on a work laptop that blocks driver installs. I found no maker statement on hinge load, so the page should not claim the lid mount is hinge-safe.

findings.label: Maker's cable order (video path)
findings.value: "If your laptop has USB-C port, please directly connect the monitor by using the USB-C to C cable." / "If your laptop does not work with USB-C to C cable, please also connect the HDMI cable to your laptop." / "If it does not work with the first two methods, please connect USB- C to C cable with USB-A adapter and HDMI cable."
findings.note: Quotes relayed by the fetch tool's reader from the opened page. The page covers the Duex Max DS only, does not use the words 'DP Alt Mode', does not say what the USB-A adapter carries, and has no driver step in the installation instructions.

findings.label: Mount instruction and hinge wording
findings.value: "Place the magnetic plates towards the monitor side and remove the adhesive stickers." The page carries no lid or hinge warning, no laptop size and no magnet count.
findings.note: The absence is as reported by the fetch tool's reader of the opened page.

findings.label: Maker FAQ: driver named for the Duex series
findings.value: The Windows fix for a Duex monitor that stopped working is to unplug the display, then uninstall and reinstall the DisplayLink driver. Mac answers point to DisplayLink downloads and "For all Mac users, please make sure your current operating system is above 10.12." Chromebook: "No driver needed for any Chrome laptop."
findings.note: The FAQ names the 'Duex Series' / 'Duex Monitor' and no specific model, so it does not say whether the DS models use DisplayLink. It has no entry on hinges, DisplayPort Alt Mode, HDMI power, Apple-silicon Macs or power draw.

findings.label: Maker FAQ: magnets are adhesive-backed and stay on the lid
findings.value: Removal: "Use a thin piece of plastic, e.g., credit to slide/wedge between the magnet and laptop lid to dislodge the adhesive." Re-attaching: "within your monitor's package box, we provide 12 additional adhesives in a packet."
findings.note: General Duex series answer, not model-specific.

findings.label: Rival page (cited by ChatGPT): weight, video path, power, fit
findings.value: "Weight: 1.3lbs"; "you can simply connect your DUEX Lite with the USB-C to C cable"; otherwise "by using a USB-C to C cable with a Type A adapter attached and an HDMI cable"; "Note: Driver required"; "Energy consumption: 4.5W"; "4x Magnetic Adhesive"; "12\" to 14\" laptops (Windows or Mac)"

findings.label: Manual: driver needed except over USB-C
findings.value: "When using USB C to connect, driver installation is not necessary." Mac: "Do not plug the Mobile Pixels Device into your mac before executing the driver installation."
findings.note: This is the older Duex Plus, not the Duex Plus DS. Useful only to show the pre-DS line shipped with a driver path. The page gives no weight or power figure.

findings.value: "check your laptop's spec sheet for “DisplayPort Alt Mode.”"; "Plenty of budget laptops have USB-C ports that only charge and move data."; "Your laptop lid and hinge have to hold the extender."; "the metal plates stay on your laptop after you take the screen off"; "Base-chip M1, M2 and M3 MacBook Pros are limited the same way, with one external screen while the lid is open." Weights it quotes: Duex Plus DS "just 1.3 pounds", Duex Max DS "1.8 pounds and 0.6 inches thick".
